title: XC983494 North American Green Treefrog
author: Paul Marvin
notes: Natural run of 17 'quonk' calls (~0.5 s apart) from one close male, building from -24 to -11 dBFS; fundamental ~1.1 kHz + harmonics to ~4 kHz. Cut in the gaps before the first and after the last call (tail kept). Faint insect bands ~6-9 kHz ~45 dB down; in-band SNR ~44 dB. 24-bit/48 kHz WAV source. Recorded River Lakes Conservation Area near Viera, Brevard Co., Florida, 2017-08-01.

title: XC978638 North American Green Treefrog
author: Paul Marvin
notes: Clean crescendo series of 21 honks from one male (starts soft and quick, ends loud ~0.45 s apart); fundamental ~1.35 kHz. Very quiet background (faint insects >6 kHz); in-band SNR ~45 dB. 24-bit/48 kHz WAV source. Recorded Viera Wetlands, Brevard Co., Florida, 2013-08-25.

title: XC983489 North American Green Treefrog
author: Paul Marvin
notes: Series of ~20 loud honks from one close male, slow at first then faster (~0.35 s apart); fundamental ~1.3 kHz. Caveat: steady low rumble below ~500 Hz in the source - keep the hp at 800 Hz; a steady insect line ~3.6 kHz sits ~30 dB under the calls. In-band SNR ~33 dB. Recorded A. R. M. Loxahatchee National Wildlife Refuge, Palm Beach Co., Florida, 2015-07-17.

title: NPS Sound Gallery - American Green Tree Frog (Everglades National Park)
author: NPS / Theresa Thom
notes: Everglades NP: two green treefrogs calling antiphonally (one loud, one a little softer), a call every ~0.25 s - a same-species duet rather than a lone frog. Source is already band-limited (~300 Hz-7 kHz, 128k MP3), so slightly duller than the XC takes. Cut at gaps (file starts mid-call). In-gap SNR ~27 dB.

title: XC982931 Squirrel Treefrog
author: Paul Marvin
notes: Five raspy 'waaak' calls (~0.25 s each, ~0.7 s apart, last after a 1.7 s pause) from one close male; energy 1.1-4.5 kHz. Faint steady insect line ~3.9 kHz well below. In-band SNR ~40 dB. 24-bit WAV. Recorded River Lakes Conservation Area near Viera, Brevard Co., Florida, 2018-05-09.

title: XC975801 Squirrel Treefrog
author: Paul Marvin
notes: Train of 11 raspy calls ~0.5 s apart from one close male (a softer second squirrel treefrog audible between, same species). Insects ~8 and ~13 kHz far below. In-band SNR ~41 dB. Recorded River Lakes Conservation Area near Viera, Brevard Co., Florida, 2016-08-12.

title: XC975801 Squirrel Treefrog
author: Paul Marvin
notes: Another full train of 12 'waaak' calls (louder take, -12 dBFS peaks) with clean gaps; faint same-species calls before/after. In-band SNR ~43 dB. Recorded River Lakes Conservation Area near Viera, Brevard Co., Florida, 2016-08-12.

title: XC975801 Squirrel Treefrog
author: Paul Marvin
notes: Train of 14 calls with a slightly irregular rhythm; a faint low note from another frog (~600-900 Hz, ~40 dB down) at 1-2 s into the clip - hp 900 removes it. In-band SNR ~43 dB. Recorded River Lakes Conservation Area near Viera, Brevard Co., Florida, 2016-08-12.

title: XC890990 Barking Treefrog
author: Chris Harrison
notes: Two barking treefrogs answering each other: 10 hollow 'toonk' calls (each a downswept stack 2 kHz->~420 Hz, energy mostly 350-500 Hz), ~0.6 s apart, the louder male at -17 dBFS in-band. IMPORTANT: a dense chorus of another species (sounds like southern cricket frogs) fills 2-4.5 kHz at about the same broadband level as the barks, so this clip needs the low-pass ('lp': 1700) as well as the hp. With

title: XC890990 Barking Treefrog
author: Chris Harrison
notes: Second run from the same pair: 10 'toonk' calls ~0.6 s apart, alternating loud/soft males. Same caveat: needs 'lp': 1700 to remove the 2-4.5 kHz cricket-frog chorus; in-band (250-1200 Hz) SNR ~41 dB. Recorded Tallahassee, Leon Co., Florida, 2022-05-22.

title: NPS Sound Gallery - Pig Frog (Everglades National Park)
author: NPS
notes: Everglades NP: two loud, close pig-frog grunts (~0.15 s each, 0.25 s apart), fundamental ~300 Hz with harmonics to ~3 kHz, natural decay. Source has low rumble below ~150 Hz (grunt energy starts ~210 Hz) - hp 150 removes it (hp 100 also fine but leaves some rumble). Short (1.95 s) but very clean; ~50 dB above the floor in 200-2500 Hz. Source is low-passed ~5 kHz.

title: XC894000 Pig Frog
author: Chris Harrison
notes: Close double grunt ('oink-oink', two 0.2 s grunts), energy 220-600 Hz + harmonics. Background: a distant pig-frog chorus (same species) and faint other-frog/insect bands at 2.2 and 3.6 kHz about 25 dB down. In-band SNR ~26 dB. 320k MP3. Recorded Miami, Miami-Dade Co., Florida, 2018-05-18.

title: XC894000 Pig Frog
author: Chris Harrison
notes: Second close double grunt from the same male, slightly longer, same background (distant same-species chorus). In-band SNR ~27 dB. Recorded Miami, Miami-Dade Co., Florida, 2018-05-18.

title: XC982868 Pig Frog
author: Paul Marvin
notes: Run of three pulsed grunts (~0.15 s each, 0.35 s apart) from a close male over a distant pig-frog chorus (same species). ~31 dB above the chorus floor in 180-2500 Hz. 24-bit WAV. Recorded River Lakes Conservation Area near Viera, Brevard Co., Florida, 2018-06-13.

title: XC982868 Pig Frog
author: Paul Marvin
notes: Run of six grunts (~0.2 s each, ~0.3 s apart) from a close male, the classic pig-frog grunting run, over the same distant same-species chorus. ~30 dB above the floor in band. Recorded River Lakes Conservation Area near Viera, Brevard Co., Florida, 2018-06-13.

title: XC984171 Southern Leopard Frog
author: Paul Marvin
notes: Full southern leopard frog 'chuckle': a run of rapid pulsed croaks (4 s) ending in a croak and two short clucks. Energy 300 Hz-2.5 kHz. A faint mixed chorus (squiggles 2-4 kHz) sits ~35 dB down. 24-bit WAV. Recorded Orlando Wetlands, Christmas, Orange Co., Florida, 2017-04-02.

title: XC984171 Southern Leopard Frog
author: Paul Marvin
notes: Shorter chuckle: two pulsed bursts, a croak, then two clucks; same male. ~35 dB above the floor in band. Recorded Orlando Wetlands, Christmas, Orange Co., Florida, 2017-04-02.

title: XC984171 Southern Leopard Frog
author: Paul Marvin
notes: A different call type: five separate guttural croaks (~0.3 s each, irregular spacing), slightly softer than clips 1-2. ~34 dB above the floor in band. Recorded Orlando Wetlands, Christmas, Orange Co., Florida, 2017-04-02.

title: iNaturalist observation 286459837 (sound 1502365)
author: Nate N. (iNaturalist: spinifer)
notes: Loud, clean single trill, 7.6 s, ~1.75 kHz (+ harmonics), with natural onset and stop; steady insect line ~5.4 kHz ~35 dB below. A few low thumps (<500 Hz) in the source - hp 700 removes them. ~45 dB above the floor in band. 192k MP3. Recorded Putnam Co., Florida, 2025-03-30 21:08.

title: XC890997 Southern Toad
author: Chris Harrison
notes: Close trill, 8.9 s, ~2.2 kHz with harmonics (A-rated), over a quieter background trill from another toad. Caveat: the source is a 22 kHz / 64k MP3 (top end ~11 kHz), fine for a 2 kHz trill. Close trill ~19 dB over the background trill. Recorded Woods and Lakes, Marion Co., Florida, 2018-05-15.

title: iNaturalist observation 270694485 (sound 1376989)
author: Aaron Stoll (iNaturalist: aaron567)
notes: Short trill (~3.2 s) rising slightly to ~2.2 kHz, with a clean stop. Source has strong rumble below ~400 Hz - keep hp 700. ~44 dB above the floor in band. MP3. Recorded Pensacola, Escambia Co., Florida, 2025-04-14 22:04.

title: XC890995 Oak Toad
author: Chris Harrison
notes: Five clear chick-like peeps (~0.25 s downslurred whistles at ~4.5 kHz, harmonic ~9 kHz), ~0.6-1.5 s apart. Soft broadband background (1-4 kHz) ~40 dB down; hp 2500 cleans it. A-rated, ~37 dB SNR. Recorded Naples, Collier Co., Florida, 2018-05-15.

title: XC890995 Oak Toad
author: Chris Harrison
notes: Five more peeps from the same male, a different rhythm (three quick, a pause, two). ~38 dB SNR. Recorded Naples, Collier Co., Florida, 2018-05-15.

title: XC984004 Oak Toad
author: Paul Marvin
notes: Three bursts of rapid peeps (4-5 peeps each at ~4 kHz) from a close oak toad with others joining softly; very quiet background. ~56 dB above the floor in band. 24-bit WAV, A-rated. Recorded River Lakes Conservation Area near Viera, Brevard Co., Florida, 2018-05-09.

title: XC984004 Oak Toad
author: Paul Marvin
notes: Five peep-bursts from the same chorus (3-5 peeps each), a busier stretch with two toads overlapping (same species). ~54 dB SNR. Recorded River Lakes Conservation Area near Viera, Brevard Co., Florida, 2018-05-09.

title: XC983538 Southern Cricket Frog
author: Paul Marvin
notes: Slow opening of a cricket-frog call: 8 sharp 'gick' clicks ~1 s apart at ~3.6 kHz. Background a faint insect band 6-10 kHz far below; ~60 dB above the floor in band. 24-bit WAV, A-rated. Recorded Buck Lake Conservation Area, Mims, Brevard Co., Florida, 2018-06-25.

title: XC983538 Southern Cricket Frog
author: Paul Marvin
notes: The same call series accelerating into dense double and triple clicks, the classic cricket-frog build-up, ending naturally. ~60 dB SNR. Recorded Buck Lake Conservation Area, Mims, Brevard Co., Florida, 2018-06-25.

title: XC983540 Southern Cricket Frog
author: Paul Marvin
notes: Three short rapid click bursts (5-7 clicks each, ~0.18 s apart) at ~3.7 kHz from another individual, separated by natural pauses. A soft periodic note from another frog (~1.1 kHz) ~40 dB down; hp 1300 removes it. ~46 dB SNR. Recorded River Lakes Conservation Area near Viera, Brevard Co., Florida, 2017-07-22.
